title: The Illiterate Who Set Up for a Schoolmaster
logline: A mosque servant who cannot read puts on an enormous turban, opens a school, and bluffs his way through a letter he holds upside down.
moral: A big turban is not knowledge: people who judge by appearance are easily fooled, and a bold bluffer may get away with it.
tone: Dry comedy of pretence. The audience is always ahead of the characters: the page is upside down, the children do the teaching, the turban does the work.

beats.summary: A mosque servant cannot read or write.
But he is good at fooling people (wink to camera).
He decides to open a school for children.
He hangs tablets (one upside down) and puts on an enormous turban.
Passers-by take the turban for learning and send their children.
He only points; the children teach one another.
A woman arrives with a letter from her travelling husband.
He tries to escape and cannot (the turban jams in the window).
He holds the page upside down.
His worried head-shaking makes her think her husband is dead.
She asks about mourning; he nods yes without knowing a word.
The neighbour has news: the husband is well.
The real letter: well, back in ten days, a quilt and a candle snuffer.
She is furious and marches back.
He will not confess; he invents an answer.
The absurd picture: the husband rolled dead in the quilt beside the snuffer.
Strangest of all, she accepts it.
He stays in his school under the turban, safe from the question.

sets.description: marketStreet strip w 2400, palette 'clear', preset 'day', palace:false, no stalls except one fruit stall at x 1000 for life. Custom house fronts left to right (ground y 900): the woman's house x 250..600 (wall top y 430, door x 350..490 top y 620, one doorstep 20 high drawn by the scene as her seat); the neighbour's house x 620..900 (wall top y 400, shuttered window 120 x 130 centred (760, 575), sill y 640, door x 800..880); school front x 1250..1650 (the planned 'school front': wall top y 380, arched door x 1380..1520 top y 610, sign board 240 x 70 on two chains centred (1450, 520)); mosque front x 1900..2350 (new small piece mosqueFront: wall top y 420, pointed door x 2050..2190 top y 600, dome r 110 centred (2120, 420) with a crescent finial, slim minaret 60 wide from y 900 up to y 200 at x 2300). Camera uses camX (left edge). All positions are a specification for custom fronts; measure against marketStreet anchors when built.

The planned kuttab dressing of palaceHall variant 'merchant' (AN-123, AN-149): wall 'ochre', door with a leaf at the left (about x 60..190, top y 560; approximate, measure on the set anchors MERCHANT.door), no desk, no shelves, curtain 0 and no treasure, floor y 900. Dressing for this film: window in the right part of the back wall x 840..950, y 470..620 (110 wide, pass as window: [840, 470, 110, 150] or draw with townWindow); five wall nails at y 430 for tablets at x 300, 400, 500, 600, 700 (tablets 70 x 95, centres y 470), two pinned papers at (350, 610) and (550, 610); teacher cushion (floorCushion 120 x 36) at x 740; lesson stand (X-frame 90 high with a 150 x 200 lesson tablet) at x 610, drawn smaller (0.6) so it does not hide the teacher; four pupil mats (140 x 40 striped ovals) at x 200, 300, 400, 500 with y 900, 880, 900, 880; a stool at x 760 in S3 only (it holds the turban). Empty (no mats, no stand) in S3.

The inside of the letter as a full-panel picture, using the planned letterFrame (rollers 972 x 34 top and bottom, paper margin, red seal lower right). Paper ground #fbf2da with six faint blue squiggle text lines (y 420..720, they part like curtains at the open), a ground line at y 820 with two small dunes, a house icon 90 x 90 at x 900. No sky. Cheap: one bake.

props.description: Enormous white turban, 180 wide x 125 tall at s 1 (the head is about 64 wide): five overlapping wrap bands with blue Ben-Day shading, red jewel r 9 front centre, yellow feather 60 long, a hanging tail 50 long at the back. Loose prop (on the stool, in the hands) and worn over the servant cap. Fields: wob (rotation, lagging the head), slump -1..1 (slides forward and sideways; at 1 it covers both eyes), hopY.

The letter: cream sheet 90 x 120 in the hand, 520 x 700 as an insert. Top: a round portrait of the husband (the planned portraitMedallion idea, r 14 in hand size, r 80 in the insert) so that upside down reads at once; six squiggle lines (right-aligned, like Arabic); red wax seal r 8 at the bottom left. Fields: rot (Math.PI = upside down), fold 0..1, crumple 0..1 (corner creases), read 0..1 (lines light up right to left, top to bottom), portrait gaze.

The planned school tablet (AN-123, AN-149): wooden board with a handle tab at the top, four ink bands that write on, lesson state. Hand size 70 x 95, lesson size 150 x 200. Used hung on the wall (one with rot Math.PI), stacked, in pupils' hands and as the teacher's screen.

Thick patchwork quilt: flat 300 x 150 with 4 x 3 patches (red, blue, yellow, white with dots), scalloped stitched border. Fields: unroll 0..1 (from a tied bundle 110 x 90) and wrap 0..1 (rolls round a lying figure 240 long into a cylinder 260 x 100 with a spiral end, three turns, the head left out).

Brass candle snuffer: a small cone (bell) 34 wide x 40 tall on a curved arm with a straight handle 120 long, yellow with red dot shading and a glint. Field dip 0..1 lowers the cone over a flame. Comes with the planned candle (stick 20 x 70, flame, flicker, out state with a smoke curl).
Library thought cloud: the parents' mistaken belief (S4), the far husband (S6), the imagined death (S8), the neighbour's news (S11) and the impostor's told picture (S15, 540 x 330).

subtitles.ar: كان في خدمة مسجد رجل لا يعرف القراءة ولا الكتابة، لكنه يجيد|خداع الناس. قرر يومًا أن يفتح|مدرسة للصغار، فجمع ألواحًا وأوراقًا وعلقها على الجدران، ثم لبس عمامة كبيرة.
subtitles.en: A mosque servant who could neither read nor write|decided to open a school.|He hung up tablets and papers and put on a large turban.

subtitles.ar: ظن المارة أن صاحب العمامة عالم كبير،|فأرسلوا أبناءهم إليه.|كان يشير إلى طفل ويقول اكتب، وإلى آخر ويقول اقرأ،|بينما يتعلم الأطفال من بعضهم، ولا يشرح المعلم شيئًا بنفسه.
subtitles.en: Passersby mistook his appearance for scholarship|and enrolled their children.|He told one child to write and another to read,|while the pupils taught one another.

subtitles.ar: ذات يوم جاءت امرأة تحمل رسالة من زوجها المسافر.|أراد الرجل الهرب قبل أن تطلب قراءتها، لكنه لم يستطع.|ناولته الورقة وسألته عما كتب زوجها،|فأمسكها مقلوبة أمام عينيه.
subtitles.en: One day a woman arrived with a letter from her traveling husband.|Unable to escape,|the impostor held the page upside down|and pretended to read.

subtitles.ar: أخذ يهز رأسه ويظهر القلق،|فخافت المرأة وظنت أن زوجها مات.|سألته هل تمزق ثيابها وتلطم وجهها حزنًا،|فأجابها بالموافقة، من غير أن يعرف كلمة واحدة في الرسالة.
subtitles.en: He shook his head and looked distressed.|The woman assumed her husband had died;|when she asked whether to tear her clothes and beat her face,|he agreed.

subtitles.ar: رجعت المرأة إلى بيتها تبكي مع أطفالها.|سمع جارها الخبر، فقال إنه تلقى بالأمس رسالة من زوجها تؤكد أنه بخير وسيعود قريبًا.|طلب الورقة وقرأ ما فيها أمامها.
subtitles.en: She returned home weeping with her children.|A neighbor who had recently heard from her husband|asked to see the letter and read it aloud.

subtitles.ar: كانت الرسالة تقول إن الزوج سليم وسيعود بعد عشرة أيام،|وإنه أرسل لحافًا وأداة لإطفاء الشموع.|غضبت المرأة، وحملت الرسالة مرة أخرى إلى المدرسة لتسأل المعلم لماذا أخافها هكذا.
subtitles.en: The husband was well and would return in ten days;|he had sent a quilt and a candle extinguisher.|Furious, the woman went back to confront the teacher.

subtitles.ar: لم يعترف الرجل بأنه أمي، بل اخترع جوابًا عجيبًا.|قال إنه ظن الزوج ميتًا ملفوفًا في اللحاف،|لأن أداة إطفاء الشموع كانت معه، وادعى أن هذا سبب حزنه عند قراءة الرسالة.
subtitles.en: Rather than admit he was illiterate, the man invented a strange explanation:|he claimed to have imagined the husband dead inside the quilt,|with the extinguisher beside him.

subtitles.ar: والأغرب أن المرأة قبلت هذا التفسير وانصرفت دون أن تكشف حيلته.|وبقي الرجل جالسًا في مدرسته بعمامته|الكبيرة، يترك الأطفال يتعلمون وحدهم، وقد نجا من سؤال كان يمكن أن يفضحه.
subtitles.en: Strangely, she accepted his excuse and left.|The impostor remained at his school in his enormous turban,|having escaped exposure once again.

new_assets.name: bigTurban
new_assets.description: Oversized turban as a loose prop and as headwear over any person head, with wob, slump and hopY (see props). Same idea as the planned judgeTurban (loose) and person headwear offset; build them as one function if possible.
new_assets.implementation: One function bigTurban(ctx, x, y, {s, wob, slump, hopY}) with origin at the brow line: five ellipse bands (K path fills, white, blue dot pattern clip on the lower half, black brush outline), jewel circle, feather as a tapered bezier with lag (swing of the head x velocity). Worn: draw after person() at the head centre (person head position: measure once from P.hands / head constants), translate by slump * (0, 26) and rotate wob about the brow.

new_assets.name: letterSheet
new_assets.description: Letter page with a portrait at the top, squiggle lines and a seal; rot, fold, crumple, read (see props). Reusable for any letter, contract or message.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rect + six seeded squiggle polylines (K.rng) + small person head clipped in a circle (portraitMedallion) + seal circle. rot via ctx.rotate about the centre. read: draw the lines again in blue up to a moving clip.

new_assets.name: writingTablet
new_assets.description: Planned school tablet (reused name): board with handle tab, ink bands, lesson state, rot.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rect in brown with a paper face, tab on top, four ink bands drawn with a length 0..1; glow = yellow stroke under the band.

new_assets.name: quilt
new_assets.description: Patchwork quilt with unroll and wrap states (see props). Reusable as any blanket, bedding or bundle.
new_assets.implementation: Flat: grid of rects with dot patterns inside a scalloped outline. unroll: clip the flat part to width * unroll and draw a shrinking spiral roll at the free edge (as the planned carpetRoll). wrap: draw the lying person, then a rounded rect 260 x 100 over the body with diagonal patch stripes sliding with wrap and a spiral at the foot end; the head is drawn after it.

new_assets.name: candleSnuffer
new_assets.description: Brass snuffer cone on a handle with dip, plus the planned candle with an out state and smoke curl.
new_assets.implementation: Cone = triangle with a rounded base, arm = quadratic stroke 8 wide, handle = rect; dip rotates the whole about the handle end. Smoke = tapered bezier growing with blend(), alpha fading.

new_assets.name: schoolRoom
new_assets.description: Planned kuttab dressing of palaceHall 'merchant' (reused name) with this film's wall tablets and right-hand window.
new_assets.implementation: palaceHall(ctx, {variant:'merchant', wall:'ochre', desk:false, shelves:false, curtain:0, treasure:false, window:[840,470,110,150]}) then the dressing drawn by the scene: floorCushion, mats (ellipses with stripes), stand (two crossed strokes + tablet), wall tablets. Bake the static dressing.

new_assets.name: townStreet fronts (school front, mosque front)
new_assets.description: Custom fronts on marketStreet: the planned school front with a sign board, two plain house fronts with a doorstep and a shuttered window, and a small mosque front (door, dome with crescent, minaret).
new_assets.implementation: marketStreet houses option for the plain fronts; townDoor and townWindow for doors and shutters; sign = S.box style board on two chain lines with swing(); dome = half ellipse with dot shading and a crescent path; minaret = tall rect with a balcony ring and a small dome.

new_assets.name: letterWorld (with letterFrame)
new_assets.description: Full-panel "inside the letter" picture using the planned letterFrame rollers and seal.
new_assets.implementation: Paper fill, squiggle lines that slide apart with open 0..1, ground line and dune arcs, house icon from three shapes; rollers drawn in panel space after the world.

new_assets.name: handOver
new_assets.description: Planned helper: an object follows hand A, then eases to hand B over 0.25 s with a weight dip; both gazes follow.
new_assets.implementation: Position = mix(handA, handB, ease(blend(t, t0, t0 + 0.25))) with a 6 unit dip pulse at arrival; use P.hands from each person.

new_assets.name: sneak
new_assets.description: Planned tiptoe option for walk(): high knees and a short hold on each toe (four steps at 50.5 to 52.3).
new_assets.implementation: walk() with a stepped distance function (hold, then move) and amp raised; body sq 1.03 on each toe hold.

new_assets.name: worryScribble

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English translation is a condensed version of the Arabic (for example P1 omits "but he was skilled at deceiving people" and "for children", P2 omits "the teacher explained nothing himself", P5 omits the neighbour's news that the husband is well, P7 omits "and claimed this was why he was sad", P8 omits "without exposing his trick" and the pupils learning alone); both are kept verbatim as supplied.
The script says only that he "could not" escape; the plan shows why with an invented gag: the enormous turban jams in the window frame (52.92, lettering STUCK!). Default: keep the gag.
The imagined death is softened: in the thought cloud and the told picture the husband simply lies down with closed eyes (no grave, no shroud beyond the comic quilt roll). Default: keep it this mild.

Tearing clothes and striking the face are shown only as a questioning mime (she grips her collar and pats her cheeks twice); after his YES she wails but nothing is torn and no blow is shown. Default: mime only.
The teacher keeps his servant tunic and only adds the giant turban, so that the turban alone fools people. Default: no scholar robe.

Invented lettering beyond sound words: CAN'T READ!, BIG TURBAN, A GREAT SCHOLAR!, WRITE!, READ!, LESSONS TAUGHT: 0, UPSIDE DOWN!, YES!, WORDS READ: 0, 10 DAYS, QUILT, SNUFFER, WHY?!, OH! I SEE. Default: keep all (about 20 items with repeats).
Added closing touch not in the script: a pupil turns the upside-down wall tablet the right way round and the turban slides over the sleeping teacher's eyes under THE END. Default: keep.
implementation_notes: Word cues: every action carries cue.t from timeline.md; use w(p, n) from timing.json and start anticipation up to 0.3 s early. The narration has almost no pauses: only 5.62-5.94, 8.72-9.28, 20.66-21.24 and 161.52-161.84 are gaps.

Sound: six quiet effects only, all in those gaps or after the last word (5.78 pop, 9.0 chime, 20.95 boing, 161.68 pop, 169.42 soft tap as the turban slides down, 170.3 chime). SND master 0.6. Do not add effects on the door slam or the window jam: there is no gap there, the picture carries them.

The page is upside down every time the impostor holds it (61.44 to 85.9, 147.42) and upright with everyone else (woman, neighbour). The portrait on the sheet is the tell; keep it at least 28 px on screen in the two-shots and use the insert at 62.58.

bigTurban always lags the head by 2 to 4 frames (wob) and is the one moving thing when he pretends to be still. Explicit lid values override LIFE auto-blink: add blink(t, seed) by hand wherever lid is set.
